newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Arkwright field on stream early - Amoco.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Arkwright field on stream early - Amoco.

text.p: Amoco Corp said on Monday its Arkwright oilfield in the central North Sea came on stream on Sunday, two weeks ahead of schedule.
The field, in block 22/23a about 150 miles east of Aberdeen, will intitially produce about 8,000 barrels per day (bpd) to be exported via the Forties pipeline system.
"It is soon expected to exceed its design rate of 12,000 bpd," said Amoco (U.K.) Exploration Company, Arkwright operator and owner of a 30.77 percent stake.
Other equity holders are Amerada Hess Ltd with 28.2 percent and Enterprise Oil Ltd with 41.03 percent.
Development costs are expected to undershoot initial estimates of 57 million stg by one or two percent, Amoco said.

"The Arkwright development leverages our existing investment in Northern North Sea infrastructure which allows us to develop incremental reserves for low cost and extend the life of our existing assets," said Amoco North Sea resource development manager Craig Wiggs.
Arkwright has been developed on a fast track since the British government granted Amoco approval in December 1995.
It will be tied back via a subsea pipeline system to the existing Amoco-operated Arbroath platform, seven miles away.
